findings.title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so a group with exactly 50 members and limit 50 reports 2 pages instead of 1 (100 members reports 3 instead of 2). Because showingLast compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the Next control stays enabled on the real last page; the next action then sets offset to user_count and findMembers returns an empty member list, leaving the admin on a phantom empty page.

findings.title: Group creation silently discards the alias_level chosen in the UI
findings.body: Discourse.Group#asJSON sends name, alias_level and visible, and the admin form exposes the alias-level combo box even for a new group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible. Any alias level selected before first saving a group is therefore lost and the group is persisted with the database default of 0 (nobody), with no error shown to the admin.

findings.title: Public group members page is now silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination
findings.body: The members endpoint now always applies limit (default 50) and offset, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned all members. The public discourse/templates/group/members.hbs template gained no next/previous controls (pagination was only added to the admin template), so for any group with more than 50 members the public members page silently shows only the first 50 in username order and the remaining members are unreachable.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset parameters
findings.body: limit and offset are taken straight from params with only to_i coercion. Any user who can view a group can request limit=1000000 to force the server to serialize the entire membership in one response (defeating the new pagination and enabling an expensive request), and a negative limit or offset is passed to ActiveRecord/PostgreSQL, producing a 500 error instead of a clamped or rejected value. The values should be clamped to a sane range (e.g. limit between 1 and a fixed maximum, offset >= 0).

findings.title: findMembers no longer returns a promise when the group name is empty
findings.body: findMembers previously returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) for a nameless group, so callers could safely chain .then() on the result. It now returns undefined in that branch while returning an ajax promise otherwise, breaking the method's contract; any caller that chains off the return value (including the next/previous actions in the admin group controller, which return group.findMembers()) will throw a TypeError for a group without a name.

findings.title: remove_member spec exercises the wrong HTTP verb and cannot catch a routing break
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member (and the client in group.js issues a DELETE). Controller specs bypass routing, so this test passes even if the DELETE route is broken or removed, and it misleadingly documents PUT as the removal verb while the sibling success example on line 125 uses DELETE.
